observation: Self-inflicted rework: the orchestrator escalated a nullable `tasks.threadId` into an 'architecture violation', which drove an entire Increment 0 — migration SQL, backfill, NOT NULL constraint, adopt guard, PGlite-vs-Postgres analysis, real-data desktop smoke, task-creation-path enumeration — all of which was deleted wholesale at rev 4. The premise was wrong: threads resolve by `(hostKind, hostId)` lookup, so no host needs an FK column at all.

Only the round-2 critique flagged the contradiction — and noted the irony that feasibility was the correct one.

It also raised the score from 6.2 to 7.1 with per-dimension traceability.

observation: The first live-harness proof was a FALSE GREEN: it asserted only that SOME message authored by the assistant's id existed in the thread. Increment 5 of the same work package added a never-silent notice authored as that SAME agent id, so a turn that failed to reply and got caught by the safety net satisfied the assertion identically to a real reply. Two features shipped in one WP whose outputs were indistinguishable to the assertion — the general shape is: an existence assertion plus a second producer of the same artifact.
evidence: commit 932e479b (test(AU27): strengthen the Increment 8 reply proof against the never-silent-notice false green); packages/core-api/src/__tests__/assistant-reply-live-harness.integration.test.ts:311-325

observation: The false green was caught by a human/orchestrator running the harness lane manually and reading the logs — not by any automated gate. `check`, `lint`, `test` and `test:integration:service` were all green with the vacuous assertion in place, and the harness lane is release-gated so per-merge verify never runs it. Nothing in the pipeline distinguishes 'the test passed' from 'the test could not have failed'.
evidence: review.md:23 ('Harness lane NOT run — release-gated… Its assertions were read line by line instead'); review.md:12-21 verification table (all gates PASS at the point the false green existed)

observation: The false green was concealing two real production bugs, both only surfaceable by an actual harness run: (1) return-action tool names were emitted bare, so `reply` was literally uncallable on opencode ('Model tried to call unavailable tool reply') because opencode's MCP client exposes it as `hyperidle_reply`; (2) the return_status tool baked `hyperidle_` into its own name, producing `hyperidle_hyperidle_return_status` under opencode's namespacing — a name no model could ever call.
evidence: commit 9b411b09 (harness-literal names, 6 files); commit ec091d01 (double-prefix fix)

observation: When the false green was fixed, the builder performed a real sanity-break to prove the strengthened assertion was not vacuous: renamed the `reply` tool to an unreachable name so no harness could call it, confirmed all 3 retry attempts failed deterministically, then reverted and re-ran green. The sanity-break was documented in the commit message rather than only claimed.
evidence: commit 932e479b commit body ('Sanity-break performed manually (not committed)… All 3 retry attempts on the builtin lane failed deterministically')

observation: The independent code review found the IDENTICAL false-green pattern surviving in a sibling test the same work package had rewritten: the AU9 realbinary proof polled `messages WHERE senderId='ast-au9-real-human'` and asserted `.toBe(1)` — satisfiable by the never-silent notice. The builder fixed the pattern where it was found and did not sweep for it. The test's own prompt even asked for a literal answer ('durable handoff works') that was never asserted.
evidence: review.md:215-226 (W2); fixed only after review by commit 342b4424

observation: The independent code review caught two LIVE correctness bugs the WP introduced, not just staleness: (1) `return_status`'s static description — shown to every agent including the assistant — instructed it to call one of three tools, none of which would satisfy its `reply`-required gate; (2) `packages/eval/src/scenarios/force-return.ts` seeds instruct the agent not to call submit_review/handoff_to/send_message to drive the force path, but `reply` is now a return action in every role's registry, so a compliant agent silently defeats the eval's premise.
evidence: review.md:286-300 (W6); fixed by commit 6ddfa614

observation: The reviewer explicitly refused the 'pre-existing / out of scope' classification for a doc claim, on the correct test: the sentence was TRUE on origin/main and is FALSE on this branch because of this diff. That test — did MY diff make it false, not does it also appear on main — is the one the builder failed to apply twice in this WP.
evidence: review.md:280-281 ('I do not accept the pre-existing / out of scope classification: the sentence was true on origin/main and is false on this branch because of this diff')

observation: A builder classified a failing test as 'pre-existing' on the evidence that it also failed at our own branch HEAD — which contained all of AU27. Reproducing a failure on a branch that contains the suspected cause is not evidence of pre-existence. The dispute was only settled by cutting a scratch worktree on origin/main and running the test there, where it passed cleanly.
evidence: commit ed60f7cb body ('Root-caused against origin/main (main passes cleanly via the deleted pre-AU27 bypass — proving the failure is not pre-existing)')

observation: The scratch-worktree-on-origin/main comparison is what settled the disputed 'pre-existing' claim definitively — a cheap, mechanical, non-negotiable disambiguation that a re-run on the feature branch can never provide. It also produced the exact stack (MissingCredentialError at start-runtime.ts:137) via a temporary instrumented run.
evidence: commit ed60f7cb body

observation: A genuine production regression was nearly shipped: Increment 6 added an unconditional, unguarded `deps.resolveModel?.('fast')` to the SHARED durable drain, for every agent kind's admission. Any deployment without an `anthropic_api_key` credential (every openrouter-only setup, including the AR7-locked builtin test model) throws before admission completes; the outer catch releases the claim with no terminal write, so the request silently re-claims forever and nothing ever runs, with no error surfaced anywhere. A best-effort optimization was made fatal to admission for all six kinds.
evidence: commit ed60f7cb (fix); the regression was introduced by commit 2bc9ef81 (Increment 6, item 3)

observation: The regression was invisible to the entire test suite because every other harness test bypasses `deps.resolveModel` via the sanctioned `harnessTestResolvedModel` model seam. Exactly ONE test in the tree exercises the real `DbCredentialResolver` path, and it lives in the release-gated harness lane. The test seam that makes harness tests deterministic is itself the coverage hole for the credential-resolution path it stubs out.
evidence: commit ed60f7cb @lore block in start-runtime.ts ('the only harness test exercising the real DbCredentialResolver path — every other harness test bypasses deps.resolveModel via the harnessTestResolvedModel seam')

observation: Dead guards were found and deleted in THREE separate rounds within one work package. Round 1 (commit 1dae6d7b, −1698 lines): au3-runtime-vocab-guard, au6-agent-boundary-guard, au7-runtime-retirement-guard, test-naming-guard + its 522-line allowlist, al6-naming-guard. au6 scanned `packages/server/src`, deleted work-packages ago, and printed PASS on zero files; au7's RETIRED_PATHS were all already gone.
evidence: commit 1dae6d7b

observation: Round 2 of the dead-guard cull found `au9-direct-handoff-guard.ts`, which the orchestrator had EXPLICITLY kept in round 1 with the reasoning 'enforces a real architectural invariant (import boundary)'. It enforced nothing: its only scan surface was `packages/server/src`, deleted in AU19; `files()` returns [] for a missing root, so it had read zero files and printed PASS for years. Its allowlist held 11 dead paths with five @lore blocks saying so. A deliberate keep-decision was made on the guard's stated purpose without checking whether its scan surface still existed.
evidence: review.md:308-318 (W8, reviewer ran inspect(repoRoot) directly and got []); commit 56c538cd

observation: Round 3 found inert entries in the harness coverage floor itself: `BUILTIN_ONLY_INTEGRATION` held two entries, both dead (one file does not exist; the other's path never matched via endsWith), and `EXPLICIT_HARNESS_INTEGRATION` held three more dead entries pre-dating AU27. AU27 added its OWN new file to that same list and did not notice the dead neighbours. The carve-out's justification ('the assistant cannot run a CLI harness') was disproven by AU27's own five-harness test, and it cited a test file AU27 had deleted.
evidence: review.md:322-334 (N1); commit 56c538cd

observation: Common root cause across all three dead-guard rounds: a guard resolves its scan root by path, the helper returns [] for a missing root, and the guard then prints PASS. A guard that inspected zero files is indistinguishable in the lint chain from a guard that inspected the whole tree and found nothing. No guard asserts a non-empty scan surface, and nothing ties a guard's lifetime to the lifetime of the directory it guards.
evidence: review.md:308-312 ('files() returns [] for a missing root (au9-direct-handoff-guard.ts:62); it is in the lint chain and prints au9-direct-handoff-guard: PASS'); same shape in au6/au7 per commit 1dae6d7b

observation: The whole-lane harness run gets OOM-killed; running one harness per process is required to complete the five-lane proof. This is an operational constraint on any WP whose acceptance criteria require a multi-harness live proof, and it is not encoded anywhere in the npm scripts — `npm run test:integration:harness` as documented will not complete.

observation: A new optional dependency (`resolveOrCreateCallingThread`) was made optional on all four resolvers, so dropping any one composition-root wiring degrades SILENTLY to `NO_CALLING_THREAD` with no type error and no test failure. The architecture had explicitly promised the AU21 K1 precedent — 'every composition-root resolver site gets a proof it supplies the bake, each sanity-broken' — and did not deliver it; resolver tests inject a local fake instead. AU21's K1 was itself reopened for a wiring gap of exactly this shape.
